characters.name: Sherlock Holmes
characters.note: Consulting detective, Baker Street; narrator's companion.

characters.name: Watson
characters.note: First-person narrator, Holmes's friend and chronicler, a doctor.

characters.name: John Openshaw
characters.note: Young visitor from Horsham; nephew of Colonel Openshaw and son of Joseph Openshaw; killed near Waterloo Bridge.

characters.name: Colonel Elias Openshaw
characters.note: John's uncle, former Confederate colonel and Florida planter; died in a garden pool in 1883.

characters.name: Joseph Openshaw
characters.note: John's father, Coventry bicycle-tire patentee; died after falling into a chalk-pit in 1885.

characters.name: Major Prendergast
characters.note: Mentioned by John; Holmes once saved him in the Tankerville Club scandal.

characters.name: Major Freebody
characters.note: Commander of a fort on Portsdown Hill; Joseph Openshaw's friend.

characters.name: Mr. Fordham
characters.note: Horsham lawyer who witnessed the colonel's will.

characters.name: Police-Constable Cook
characters.note: Heard the cry near Waterloo Bridge; only in the newspaper report.

characters.name: Captain James Calhoun
characters.note: Master of the barque Lone Star; Holmes's target; only mentioned.

characters.name: K. K. K.
characters.note: Secret society whose warnings take the form of orange pips; treated as a group that pursues the family.

characters.name: Hudson
characters.note: Named only in the colonel's diary entry, as a man who came.

characters.name: McCauley
characters.note: Named in the colonel's diary as a man marked with pips and later cleared.

characters.name: Paramore
characters.note: Named in the colonel's diary as a man visited.

characters.name: John Swain
characters.note: Named in the colonel's diary as a man of St. Augustine who was marked and cleared.

characters.name: Cuvier
characters.note: Cited by Holmes as an example of deduction from a single bone.

locations.name: Baker Street
locations.note: Holmes and Watson's rooms, where the interview and later scenes take place.

locations.name: Horsham
locations.note: Sussex town where the Openshaw estate lies.

locations.name: Coventry
locations.note: Where Joseph Openshaw's factory stood; mentioned only.

locations.name: Florida
locations.note: Colonel Openshaw's American plantation; mentioned only.

locations.name: Portsdown Hill
locations.note: Site of Major Freebody's fort, where Joseph Openshaw was visiting; mentioned only.

locations.name: Waterloo Bridge
locations.note: Where John Openshaw's body was recovered from the Thames.

locations.name: Waterloo Station
locations.note: Railway station John took to return to Horsham; mentioned only.

locations.name: Pondicherry
locations.note: Postmark of the first letter; mentioned only.

locations.name: Dundee
locations.note: Postmark of the second letter; mentioned only.

locations.name: Savannah
locations.note: Destination port of the Lone Star; mentioned only.

brief.era: 1880s, Victorian England; the story's flashbacks reach back to the American South around 1869 and the Reconstruction era.
brief.place: Baker Street, London, with Horsham in Sussex as the family seat; scenes also reach Waterloo Bridge on the Thames and the American South.
brief.dress: Victorian middle-class and professional dress: frock coats, waterproofs and umbrellas for John Openshaw, pince-nez, and the colonel's Southern planter bearing.
brief.buildings_and_objects: Gaslit Baker Street sitting room with fireplace and violin; a lumber-room attic with a brass box; a garden sundial and a green-scummed pool; a Thames embankment; a sailing barque; dried orange pips and their envelopes; blue-tinted paper page from a diary.
depiction_rules: The K. K. K. society should be suggested through the orange pips, letters and envelopes rather than shown as a group of figures.
Hooded Klan imagery should be avoided; the society's threat is conveyed by its symbols.
The colonel's death and John's death should be shown without gratuitous violence, consistent with the accidental verdicts.
The Lone Star is seen only as a sailing barque at sea or as its shattered stern-post, never with identifiable crew.
Holmes and Watson are shown in their Baker Street room, with the storm visible through the windows.
